key_insight: DFT screening identifies condition-dependent routes to stabilize otherwise equilibrium-inaccessible MXenes using temperature, pressure, or carbon chemical potential.
engineering_relevance: The dataset links candidate MXenes to synthesis conditions, helping prioritize experimental discovery and support future machine-learned stability predictors.
method: Model 1,040 ordered binary and ternary bare, delaminated MXenes using r²SCAN DFT.
Calculate formation and decomposition Gibbs energies, decomposition products, layer symmetries, and energies above the hull.
Evaluate stabilization under elevated temperature, high pressure, and varied carbon chemical potential.
evidence_signal: The calculations identify 115 predominantly carbide MXenes stabilized at 500–2000 K, 23 at 10 GPa, and three Mn–Fe–C MXenes within experimentally feasible carbon chemical potentials.
watch_item: Predicted thermodynamic stabilization does not establish synthesis feasibility; kinetics and surface terminations are not addressed by the bare-MXene dataset.
paper_title: High-Fidelity In Silico Dataset of Ordered Binary and Ternary MXenes with Predictive Synthesis Guidance
